title: 1 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 24 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 24.

questions.question: Where was David when it was told Saul about his location?
options: In the wilderness of Engedi
In the city of Jerusalem
In the plains of Moab
In the mountains of Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: In the wilderness of Engedi
questions.explanation: The verse states that it was told Saul, "Behold, David is in the wilderness of Engedi" (1 Samuel 24:1).

questions.question: How many chosen men did Saul take to seek David?
options: Three thousand
One thousand
Five thousand
Two thousand
questions.correctAnswer: Three thousand
questions.explanation: Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel to seek David (1 Samuel 24:2).

questions.question: Where did Saul find a cave into which he entered?
options: By the sheepcotes on the way
Near the river Jordan
In the valley of Jezreel
At the top of Mount Carmel
questions.correctAnswer: By the sheepcotes on the way
questions.explanation: Saul came to the sheepcotes by the way, where there was a cave, and he went in (1 Samuel 24:3).

questions.question: What did David do secretly while Saul was in the cave?
options: Cut off the skirt of Saul's robe
Took Saul's sword
Killed one of Saul's men
Set fire to the cave
questions.correctAnswer: Cut off the skirt of Saul's robe
questions.explanation: David arose and cut off the skirt of Saul's robe privily (1 Samuel 24:4).

questions.question: True or False: David felt no remorse after cutting off Saul's robe skirt.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David's heart smote him because he had cut off Saul's skirt (1 Samuel 24:5).

questions.question: What reason did David give for not harming Saul?
options: Because Saul was the LORD'S anointed
Because Saul was his father
Because Saul was weak
Because Saul begged for mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Because Saul was the LORD'S anointed
questions.explanation: David said he would not stretch forth his hand against his master, the LORD'S anointed (1 Samuel 24:6).

questions.question: True or False: David allowed his servants to attack Saul while he was in the cave.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David stayed his servants and suffered them not to rise against Saul (1 Samuel 24:7).

questions.question: What did David do after Saul left the cave?
options: He arose, went out, and bowed before Saul
He immediately fled to another city
He sent men to spy on Saul
He shouted to his men to attack
questions.correctAnswer: He arose, went out, and bowed before Saul
questions.explanation: David arose afterward, went out of the cave, cried after Saul, and bowed himself (1 Samuel 24:8).

questions.question: Who told Saul that David was in the wilderness of Engedi?
options: It was told him by others
David himself told Saul
An angel appeared to Saul
Saul's men guessed the location
questions.correctAnswer: It was told him by others
questions.explanation: The text says it was told Saul, indicating others informed him (1 Samuel 24:1).

questions.question: True or False: Saul went into the cave to rest and cover his feet.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Saul went into the cave to cover his feet, which implies to rest (1 Samuel 24:3).

questions.question: What did the men of David say would happen that day?
options: The LORD would deliver Saul into David's hand
David would be defeated by Saul
Saul would escape unharmed
The Philistines would attack
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD would deliver Saul into David's hand
questions.explanation: They said, "Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand" (1 Samuel 24:4).

questions.question: In what location did Saul seek David and his men?
options: Upon the rocks of the wild goats
In the valley of Elah
By the seashore
In the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: Upon the rocks of the wild goats
questions.explanation: Saul sought David upon the rocks of the wild goats (1 Samuel 24:2).

questions.question: What was David's posture when he bowed to Saul after coming out of the cave?
options: He stooped with his face to the earth
He stood tall and waved
He knelt on one knee
He sat down on a rock
questions.correctAnswer: He stooped with his face to the earth
questions.explanation: David stooped with his face to the earth and bowed himself (1 Samuel 24:8).

questions.question: Sequence question: Which event happened first in 1 Samuel 24?
options: Saul enters the cave to cover his feet
David cuts off the skirt of Saul's robe
David bows to Saul after coming out of the cave
Saul takes three thousand men to seek David
questions.correctAnswer: Saul takes three thousand men to seek David
questions.explanation: The order is: Saul takes men (verse 2), Saul enters the cave (verse 3), David cuts the skirt (verse 4), then David bows to Saul (verse 8).

questions.question: True or False: David immediately killed Saul when he found him vulnerable in the cave.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David cut off the skirt of Saul's robe but did not kill him, respecting that Saul was the LORD'S anointed (1 Samuel 24:4-6).

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 24 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 24:9, what does David ask Saul about the words he hears?
options: Why do you believe that David seeks to harm you?
Why do you trust the prophets instead of me?
Why do you ignore the counsel of your men?
Why have you come to the wilderness of Engedi?
questions.correctAnswer: Why do you believe that David seeks to harm you?
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 24:9, David questions Saul by asking, 'Wherefore hearest thou men's words, saying, Behold, David seeketh thy hurt?' showing David's concern about false accusations against him. This is linked to the context of Saul pursuing him unjustly (1 Samuel 24:11).

questions.question: How does David explain his decision not to harm Saul in 1 Samuel 24:10?
options: He fears Saul's army will retaliate.
He respects Saul as the LORD's anointed and chooses not to stretch forth his hand against him.
He believes Saul will eventually repent.
He plans to negotiate peace instead.
questions.correctAnswer: He respects Saul as the LORD's anointed and chooses not to stretch forth his hand against him.
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states David's reasoning: 'I will not put forth mine hand against my lord; for he is the LORD'S anointed,' highlighting David's respect and obedience to God's appointment, despite Saul's pursuit (1 Samuel 24:6).

questions.question: What evidence does David present to Saul to show he did not intend to harm him, as described in 1 Samuel 24:11?
options: He shows Saul the sword he used to kill a lion.
He presents Saul's crown as proof.
He displays the skirt of Saul's robe which he had cut off but did not kill him.
He brings Saul's men as witnesses.
questions.correctAnswer: He displays the skirt of Saul's robe which he had cut off but did not kill him.
questions.explanation: David holds up the skirt of Saul's robe cut off in the cave to demonstrate he spared Saul's life intentionally, proving innocence and lack of sin against him (1 Samuel 24:4, 24:11).

questions.question: How does David appeal to God's justice in his conflict with Saul, according to 1 Samuel 24:12?
options: He asks God to grant him power to defeat Saul.
He says the LORD will judge and avenge between him and Saul but his hand will not be against Saul.
He requests God to remove Saul from the throne.
He promises to build a temple for the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: He says the LORD will judge and avenge between him and Saul but his hand will not be against Saul.
questions.explanation: David entrusts judgment and vengeance to God, refusing to personally harm Saul, demonstrating faith and integrity (1 Samuel 24:12, 24:6).

questions.question: What proverb does David cite in 1 Samuel 24:13 to describe the nature of wickedness?
options: A soft answer turneth away wrath.
Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked.
Pride goeth before destruction.
A wise man feareth and departeth from evil.
questions.correctAnswer: Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked.
questions.explanation: David quotes an ancient proverb to show that evil originates from the wicked, contrasting his own innocence and refusal to harm Saul (1 Samuel 24:13).

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 24:14, David compares Saul to which of the following animals to emphasize Saul's futile pursuit?
options: A lion and a bear
A dead dog and a flea
A serpent and a scorpion
A wolf and a fox
questions.correctAnswer: A dead dog and a flea
questions.explanation: David uses the imagery of a dead dog and a flea to illustrate the insignificance of Saul’s pursuit, highlighting Saul's misguided efforts (1 Samuel 24:14).

questions.question: What does David request God to do in 1 Samuel 24:15 in his conflict with Saul?
options: Bless Saul and make him strong.
Judge between David and Saul, plead David's cause, and deliver him from Saul's hand.
Grant David victory over his enemies.
Give David wisdom to rule Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: Judge between David and Saul, plead David's cause, and deliver him from Saul's hand.
questions.explanation: David asks the LORD to act as judge, advocate, and deliverer in his dispute with Saul, revealing his reliance on divine justice rather than personal vengeance (1 Samuel 24:12, 24:15).

questions.question: What is Saul's emotional reaction after David finishes speaking in 1 Samuel 24:16?
options: He laughed and mocked David.
He became angry and ordered a pursuit.
He recognized David's voice and wept.
He immediately crowned David king.
questions.correctAnswer: He recognized David's voice and wept.
questions.explanation: Verse 16 shows Saul's heartfelt response as he identifies David’s voice and weeps, revealing a moment of humility and sorrow (1 Samuel 24:16).

questions.question: How does Saul describe David's righteousness compared to his own in 1 Samuel 24:17?
options: David is less righteous than Saul.
David is equally righteous as Saul.
David is more righteous than Saul.
Saul makes no comment on righteousness.
questions.correctAnswer: David is more righteous than Saul.
questions.explanation: Saul acknowledges David's greater righteousness, noting David rewarded him with good while he had returned evil, expressing humility (1 Samuel 24:17).

questions.question: What reason does Saul give in 1 Samuel 24:18 for praising David's actions that day?
options: Because David made peace with the Philistines.
Because David spared Saul's life when he had the chance to kill him.
Because David gave Saul gifts.
Because David promised to be loyal forever.
questions.correctAnswer: Because David spared Saul's life when he had the chance to kill him.
questions.explanation: Saul commends David for showing kindness by not killing him when God delivered Saul into David's hand (1 Samuel 24:18).

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 24:19, what does Saul say will happen to David because of his good deed?
options: The LORD will curse David.
The LORD will reward David good.
David will have many enemies.
David will lose his kingdom.
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will reward David good.
questions.explanation: Saul expresses confidence that God will reward David for his mercy and kindness, illustrating the principle of divine blessing for righteous acts (1 Samuel 24:19).

questions.question: What does Saul predict about David's future in 1 Samuel 24:20?
options: David will be captured by the Philistines.
David will surely be king and establish the kingdom of Israel.
David will lose favor with God.
David will never rule Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: David will surely be king and establish the kingdom of Israel.
questions.explanation: Saul acknowledges God's plan for David to become king and establish Israel’s kingdom, showing Saul's acceptance of God's will (1 Samuel 24:20).

questions.question: What oath does Saul request from David in 1 Samuel 24:21?
options: That David will never fight the Philistines.
That David will not cut off Saul's descendants or destroy his name.
That David will marry Saul's daughter.
That David will give Saul's kingdom back.
questions.correctAnswer: That David will not cut off Saul's descendants or destroy his name.
questions.explanation: Saul asks David to swear by the LORD not to harm his seed or destroy his family name, showing concern for legacy and forgiveness (1 Samuel 24:21).

questions.question: What does David do in response to Saul's oath request in 1 Samuel 24:22?
options: He refuses to swear.
He swears to Saul as requested.
He asks for time to consider.
He ignores Saul and leaves immediately.
questions.correctAnswer: He swears to Saul as requested.
questions.explanation: David complies by swearing to Saul, demonstrating integrity and honoring promises even to an enemy (1 Samuel 24:22).

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Samuel 24:10, David expresses that he will put forth his hand against Saul because he is the LORD's anointed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David states explicitly in 1 Samuel 24:10 that he will not put forth his hand against Saul because Saul is the LORD's anointed, showing respect and obedience rather than aggression.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 24.

questions.question: What reason does Saul give for acknowledging David's righteousness in 1 Samuel 24:17?
options: David has rewarded him good, while Saul rewarded David evil
David has defeated Saul in battle
David has become king before Saul
David has killed Saul's enemies
questions.correctAnswer: David has rewarded him good, while Saul rewarded David evil
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 24:17, Saul admits David's righteousness because David has rewarded him good despite Saul's evil treatment of David.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 24:18, what specific action did David refrain from when the LORD delivered Saul into his hand?
options: Killing Saul
Taking Saul's crown
Capturing Saul's army
Destroying Saul's kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Killing Saul
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 24:18 states that although God delivered Saul into David's hand, David did not kill him, showing mercy.

questions.question: What proverb does David quote in 1 Samuel 24:13 to express his refusal to harm Saul?
options: Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked
Pride goeth before destruction
A soft answer turneth away wrath
A wise man will hear and increase learning
questions.correctAnswer: Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked
questions.explanation: David quotes the proverb 'Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked' in 1 Samuel 24:13 to justify not repaying evil for evil.

questions.question: How does Saul describe the pursuers he is following in 1 Samuel 24:14?
options: After a dead dog, after a flea
After a lion, after a fox
After a thief, after a robber
After a shadow, after the wind
questions.correctAnswer: After a dead dog, after a flea
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 24:14, Saul derides the pursuit of David by comparing it to chasing a 'dead dog' and a 'flea', indicating contempt.

questions.question: What does Saul request from David in 1 Samuel 24:21?
options: To swear by the LORD not to cut off his seed or destroy his name
To share the kingdom with him
To kill his enemies
To return to his father's house
questions.correctAnswer: To swear by the LORD not to cut off his seed or destroy his name
questions.explanation: Saul asks David to swear by the LORD not to harm his descendants or destroy his family name in 1 Samuel 24:21.

questions.question: What is the significance of David cutting off the skirt of Saul's robe in 1 Samuel 24:4?
options: It symbolized David sparing Saul's life
It was a sign of rebellion against Saul
It meant David claimed the throne
It was an act of theft
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolized David sparing Saul's life
questions.explanation: David cutting off Saul's robe skirt in 1 Samuel 24:4 was a covert act showing he could harm Saul but chose not to, symbolizing mercy.

questions.question: How does David address Saul when he reveals himself after leaving the cave in 1 Samuel 24:8?
options: My lord the king
Enemy of Israel
My brother
King of the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: My lord the king
questions.explanation: David respectfully addresses Saul as 'My lord the king' in 1 Samuel 24:8, acknowledging Saul's anointed position.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage thematically connects with David sparing Saul's life because he is the LORD's anointed?
options: Exodus 22:28 - Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people
Genesis 12:3 - Bless them that bless thee
Psalm 23 - The Lord is my shepherd
Proverbs 3:5 - Trust in the LORD with all thine heart
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 22:28 - Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:28 commands respect for rulers, paralleling David's respect for Saul as the LORD's anointed in 1 Samuel 24:6.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in David’s speech to Saul in 1 Samuel 24:10-13, particularly in the contrast between his actions and Saul’s pursuit?
options: Chiasmus
Parable
Hyperbole
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: David uses chiasmus in 1 Samuel 24:10-13, contrasting his mercy with Saul's aggression in a mirrored structure emphasizing moral superiority.

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning 'anointed one' is significant in this chapter and used to describe Saul?
options: Mashiach
Adonai
Elohim
Ruach
questions.correctAnswer: Mashiach
questions.explanation: 'Mashiach' means 'anointed one' in Hebrew; Saul is repeatedly called the LORD's anointed in 1 Samuel 24:6, highlighting his divinely appointed kingship.

questions.question: How does this chapter foreshadow the establishment of David’s kingdom as mentioned in 1 Samuel 24:20?
options: Saul acknowledges David will be king and the kingdom established in his hand
David immediately takes Saul's throne
The Philistines declare David as king
Samuel anoints David again
questions.correctAnswer: Saul acknowledges David will be king and the kingdom established in his hand
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 24:20, Saul predicts David’s future kingship, foreshadowing the eventual establishment of David’s reign over Israel.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the hold' refer to in 1 Samuel 24:22?
options: A stronghold or fortress where David and his men stayed
The temple in Jerusalem
Saul's palace
A Philistine camp
questions.correctAnswer: A stronghold or fortress where David and his men stayed
questions.explanation: 'The hold' in 1 Samuel 24:22 refers to a stronghold or fortified place where David and his men took refuge.

questions.question: True or False: David's men encouraged him to kill Saul when they found him in the cave.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 24:4, David's men encouraged him to kill Saul as the LORD had delivered him into his hand.

questions.question: True or False: Saul immediately punished David after discovering he had cut off the skirt of his robe.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Saul did not punish David; instead, in 1 Samuel 24:16-19, he wept and acknowledged David's righteousness.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of mercy shown by David to Saul in this chapter?
options: Matthew 5:44 - Love your enemies
Acts 2:38 - Repent and be baptized
Romans 8:28 - All things work together for good
Hebrews 11:1 - Faith is the substance of things hoped for
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 5:44 - Love your enemies
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:44 encourages loving enemies, echoing David’s mercy to Saul in 1 Samuel 24:10-12.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 24 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does David cutting off the skirt of Saul's robe in the cave reveal about his attitude toward Saul as "the LORD's anointed"?
options: David respected Saul’s divine appointment and refused to harm him despite opportunity
David intended to humiliate Saul publicly by cutting his robe
David sought to seize the throne immediately by taking Saul’s garment
David was indifferent to Saul’s status and acted out of personal revenge
questions.correctAnswer: David respected Saul’s divine appointment and refused to harm him despite opportunity
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 24:4-6 shows David cut off only a part of Saul's robe but refused to kill him, stating it was forbidden to stretch his hand against the LORD's anointed, demonstrating reverence for God's sovereign choice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly displayed when David declares, 'The LORD judge between me and thee, and the LORD avenge me of thee'?
options: God’s justice and righteous judgment
God’s mercy and forgiveness
God’s omniscience and knowledge
God’s omnipotence in battle
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice and righteous judgment
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 24:12, David entrusts judgment and vengeance to God, highlighting the attribute of divine justice as God alone is the righteous judge between man and man.

questions.question: How does Saul’s reaction to David’s words in 1 Samuel 24:16-17 reveal a recognition of David’s righteousness?
options: Saul acknowledges he has been treated unjustly and confesses David’s moral superiority
Saul rejects David’s words and continues his pursuit with anger
Saul accuses David of deceit and plots further harm
Saul dismisses David’s plea as weakness
questions.correctAnswer: Saul acknowledges he has been treated unjustly and confesses David’s moral superiority
questions.explanation: Verse 17 records Saul saying, 'Thou art more righteous than I,' recognizing that David has rewarded evil with good, indicating Saul’s awareness of David’s integrity.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about sanctification is illustrated by David’s decision not to kill Saul despite having the chance?
options: Sanctification involves obedience to God’s moral standards even under provocation
Sanctification is achieved through violent overthrow of enemies
Sanctification requires isolation from all conflict
Sanctification is a one-time event without ongoing choices
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves obedience to God’s moral standards even under provocation
questions.explanation: David’s restraint in 1 Samuel 24:6-7 shows his sanctified heart chooses obedience to God’s command respecting the LORD’s anointed, exemplifying progressive holiness in trials.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 24:1-3, what does Saul’s pursuit of David into the wilderness of Engedi illustrate in the broader redemptive narrative?
options: The ongoing conflict between God’s anointed king and the rejected king
The immediate establishment of David’s kingship without opposition
The alliance between Saul and David against their enemies
The fulfillment of David’s promise to protect Saul
questions.correctAnswer: The ongoing conflict between God’s anointed king and the rejected king
questions.explanation: These verses show Saul’s relentless pursuit of David, reflecting the tension between God’s chosen (David) and the fallen king (Saul), a motif preparing for the Messianic kingship (Luke 1:32).

questions.question: What synthesis theological insight arises from combining David’s refusal to harm Saul (1 Samuel 24:6) with his appeal to God as judge (1 Samuel 24:12)?
options: Believers trust God’s sovereign justice and refrain from personal vengeance
Believers are to execute judgment swiftly without delay
Human judgment is superior to divine judgment
God permits revenge as a human right
questions.correctAnswer: Believers trust God’s sovereign justice and refrain from personal vengeance
questions.explanation: David’s refusal to harm the LORD’s anointed and his reliance on God to judge (verses 6 and 12) teach that Christians must leave vengeance to God, reflecting Romans 12:19.

questions.question: How does David’s statement about pursuing a ‘dead dog’ and a ‘flea’ in 1 Samuel 24:14 reflect on Saul’s legitimacy as king?
options: It diminishes Saul’s royal authority and foreshadows God’s rejection of him
It elevates Saul’s status by comparing him to strong animals
It praises Saul’s power and kingship
It shows David’s disrespect without theological significance
questions.correctAnswer: It diminishes Saul’s royal authority and foreshadows God’s rejection of him
questions.explanation: David’s metaphor in verse 14 belittles Saul as unworthy prey, indicating the divine disfavor Saul faces, consistent with 1 Samuel 15:26 where God rejects Saul’s kingship.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the LORD delivering Saul into David’s hand as mentioned in 1 Samuel 24:10?
options: God’s providence and sovereignty over human events
God’s wrath and judgment exclusively
God’s silence in human affairs
God’s partiality toward Saul only
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence and sovereignty over human events
questions.explanation: David acknowledges in verse 10 that the LORD delivered Saul into his hand, showing God’s sovereign control over the circumstances shaping His redemptive plan.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about the nature of sin and repentance is suggested by David’s heart smiting him after cutting Saul’s robe in 1 Samuel 24:5?
options: True repentance involves conviction and remorse for sin even when not overtly malicious
Sin is irrelevant if no physical harm is done
Repentance is unnecessary if intentions are good
Sin does not affect the believer’s conscience
questions.correctAnswer: True repentance involves conviction and remorse for sin even when not overtly malicious
questions.explanation: David’s heart smiting in verse 5 reveals an internal conviction of sinfulness despite not killing Saul, illustrating the biblical principle of genuine repentance (Psalm 51:17).

questions.question: How does Saul’s request that David swear not to cut off his seed (1 Samuel 24:21) relate to the biblical doctrine of covenant faithfulness?
options: It emphasizes the importance of honoring promises and maintaining family lineage
It shows Saul’s desire to rebel against God’s covenant
It rejects the concept of covenant altogether
It demands immediate kingship for Saul’s descendants
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the importance of honoring promises and maintaining family lineage
questions.explanation: Saul’s plea in verse 21 requests David’s covenant oath, reflecting biblical emphasis on faithful promises and protection of God-ordained family lineages (Genesis 17:7).

questions.question: What does the narrative arc of Saul leaving and David going up to the hold (1 Samuel 24:22) signify in the broader messianic storyline?
options: The transition of divine favor from Saul to David foreshadowing Christ’s kingship
The end of all conflict in Israel’s monarchy
Saul’s restoration as king and David’s exile
David’s rejection by God
questions.correctAnswer: The transition of divine favor from Saul to David foreshadowing Christ’s kingship
questions.explanation: Verse 22 shows Saul departing defeated while David ascends to safety, symbolizing the shift of God’s anointing from Saul’s line toward David, a typology of Christ’s royal lineage (Acts 13:22-23).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that David’s mercy toward Saul was political expediency rather than genuine righteousness. What does 1 Samuel 24:11-13 actually teach about David’s motivation?
options: David acted out of a sincere respect for God's anointed and maintained a moral conscience free from evil
David was secretly plotting Saul’s downfall despite appearances
David ignored God’s command to submit to Saul
David sought to win public favor by pretending mercy
questions.correctAnswer: David acted out of a sincere respect for God's anointed and maintained a moral conscience free from evil
questions.explanation: Verses 11-13 highlight David’s assertion that he has not sinned against Saul and refuses to harm him despite persecution, showing genuine righteousness rather than political calculation (cf. Romans 12:17-21).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do verses 16-18 provide about divine election and human response?
options: God’s chosen are recognized by their righteousness and mercy, prompting even opponents to acknowledge their legitimacy
God’s election is irrelevant to human behavior
Human merit determines God’s choice for kingship
Divine election always causes immediate worldly success
questions.correctAnswer: God’s chosen are recognized by their righteousness and mercy, prompting even opponents to acknowledge their legitimacy
questions.explanation: Saul’s confession in verses 16-18 praises David's righteousness and mercy, affirming that divine election correlates with godly character and is recognized even by adversaries (Psalm 89:20-21).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is underscored by David’s declaration that he will not stretch his hand against Saul because he is the LORD’s anointed (1 Samuel 24:6)?
options: God’s sovereignty over kings and rulers
God’s indifference to earthly authority
God’s impatience with mercy
God’s favoritism toward David exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty over kings and rulers
questions.explanation: David’s respect for Saul as the LORD’s anointed in verse 6 highlights God’s sovereign authority over earthly rulers, a theme echoed in Romans 13:1.

questions.question: What synthesis doctrine emerges from David’s appeal to the proverb about wickedness in 1 Samuel 24:13 and his statement about not extending his hand against Saul?
options: Personal holiness requires abstaining from evil deeds even when confronted by wickedness
It is acceptable to return evil for evil
Wickedness should be embraced to overcome enemies
God condones vengeance by the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Personal holiness requires abstaining from evil deeds even when confronted by wickedness
questions.explanation: David cites the proverb that wickedness proceeds from the wicked but declares he will not impose harm (verse 13), teaching sanctification involves not reciprocating evil (Matthew 5:44).
